comment: Ten questions about this repository, each with the file a correct answer
has to cite. Every expected answer was checked with grep before it was
written down — the ground truth is the point, and ground truth nobody
verified is just a second opinion.
Scoring is on cited files, not on prose. That is mechanical, which is what
makes it worth automating; whether the prose is any good you read yourself.
A question can legitimately cite more files than are listed, so a hit means
the expected files are a subset of the cited ones.
The mix is deliberate. Questions 1, 4, 8 and 9 are lookups that one good
search should answer. Questions 2, 5 and 10 ask why something is the way it
is, which the model can only answer by reading around the line it found.

questions.question: Which file defines the ToolError exception, and how many places raise it?
How does this agent stop the model from reading files outside the repository, and why does it resolve the path before checking it rather than after?
questions.note: _resolve_within: resolve() collapses .. and follows symlinks, then is_relative_to.

questions.question: What happens when the model asks for a tool that does not exist?
questions.note: execute_tool_call returns an is_error result listing the available tools.

questions.question: At most how many matches does the search tool return, and what does it do when it reaches that limit?
questions.note: MAX_SEARCH_MATCHES = 50, then appends a 'stopped at 50 matches' note.

questions.question: Why does the loop put every tool result from one turn into a single user message instead of sending them separately?
questions.note: Splitting them teaches the model to stop making parallel calls; no error is raised.

questions.question: Which class wraps the Anthropic SDK and actually sends a request to the API?
questions.note: LiveClient. probe.py and __main__.py import anthropic too, but only to construct it.

questions.question: What does the replaying client verify before it will serve any recorded response?
questions.note: request_config: model, max_tokens, system, tools, output_schema — checked in __init__.

questions.question: What per-million-token prices are used to work out what a run cost?
questions.note: $5 input, $25 output, $0.50 cache read, $6.25 cache write.

questions.question: What are the fields of a final answer, and what values can confidence take?
questions.note: answer, citations, confidence; high | medium | low.

questions.question: Why is the repository root not a parameter in any tool's JSON schema?
questions.note: Bound by the harness so the model cannot choose it; the comment above TOOLS says so.
